title: Data center expansion in Georgia and Virginia faces new power and permitting challenges
summary: Data center operators in Georgia and Virginia face tighter grid scrutiny, stricter permitting and surging AI demand. See how Honeywell Technologies Forge helps.
body_markdown:
Data center operators building in Georgia and Virginia are running into a wall that has nothing to do with their servers. Regulators want hyperscale facilities to cover more of the grid upgrade costs their facilities drive.[\[1\]](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/insights/articles/data-center-expansion-georgia-virginia-power-permitting-challenges#1) Communities are pushing back on noise, water use and land consumption. Meanwhile, AI-driven load growth is forcing utilities to redraw long-term planning assumptions almost as fast as they're written.[\[2\]](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/insights/articles/data-center-expansion-georgia-virginia-power-permitting-challenges#2)


The operators who navigate this environment successfully will be the ones who can show, not just promise, how their facilities use power.


## What Power Scrutiny Means for Data Center Operators


The consequences are showing up in permitting cycles and project budgets. Stricter zoning reviews and environmental assessments are stretching timelines.[\[3\]](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/insights/articles/data-center-expansion-georgia-virginia-power-permitting-challenges#3) New cost-allocation frameworks mean operators may take on a larger share of the infrastructure costs tied to their projects. Community opposition has prompted moratorium discussions in some jurisdictions.[\[4\]](https://www.honeywell.com/us/en/insights/articles/data-center-expansion-georgia-virginia-power-permitting-challenges#4) Projects may now face longer paths and higher stakes.


## How Honeywell Technologies Forge Supports Energy Visibility and Compliance


Power management and reporting have become strategic. Honeywell Technologies Forge is designed to give operators visibility into energy consumption, peak demand and capacity utilization. Granular data helps demonstrate regulatory compliance, support utility planning conversations and address community concerns with evidence rather than assertions.
